description: The bar chart illustrates the correlation between knowledge popularity and LLM knowledge boundary perception across three domains—Movies, Songs, and Basketball—comparing four different metrics: PopGT, PopGe, RPopGT, and RPopGe. The vertical axis represents correlation values ranging from 0 to 0.7, with increments of 0.1, while the horizontal axis categorizes the data by domain. Each domain contains four bars, with distinct patterns and colors: PopGT is shown as solid orange, PopGe as light orange with a crosshatch pattern, RPopGT as solid dark blue, and RPopGe as dark blue with a diagonal stripe pattern. In the Movies category, PopGT and PopGe have similar low correlation values (approximately 0.25 and 0.1, respectively), while RPopGT shows a moderate correlation (around 0.35) and RPopGe has the highest correlation among all (approximately 0.65). In the Songs category, PopGT and PopGe have similar values (around 0.3 and 0.1, respectively), RPopGT shows a moderate correlation (around 0.5), and RPopGe again reaches the highest value (approximately 0.7). In the Basketball category, all four metrics have low correlation values, with PopGT and PopGe at around 0.1, RPopGT at approximately 0.15, and RPopGe at around 0.25. The chart indicates that RPopGe consistently shows the highest correlation across all domains, particularly in Movies and Songs, while PopGe consistently shows the lowest values. The bars are grouped by domain, with each group containing the four metrics in the order listed, and the legend in the top right corner identifies the color and pattern for each metric.
